title: Sep 25 Results + Sep 26 Preview: When Regression Waits Another Day
summary: 88.2% accuracy on Sep 25 slate—15 wins, 2 losses, and confidence intervals holding strong

content.value:
## Sep 25 Performance: Model Dominance

The Bayesian posterior held firm yesterday. With a 15-2 record across yesterday's slate, we're observing the kind of predictive accuracy that makes you double-check your standard errors. At 88.2%, we're operating well above our season-long baseline—though as any good sabermetrician knows, small sample theater is always lurking in the wings.

## Where the Model Excelled

Our highest-confidence selections delivered exactly as projected. The Tigers pick at 60% confidence, the Rays at 60%, and particularly the Guardians-Royals analysis at 61%—all validated our pitcher-level matchup algorithms and park-adjusted run expectancy matrices. The doubleheader sweep in the Cubs-Sox series showed our ability to parse same-day variance in bullpen availability and lineup construction.

## The Braves-Marlins Miss: Variance in Action

Our lone high-confidence miss came in Atlanta's loss to Miami. At 62% confidence, this was actually our strongest projection of the day—which makes it a perfect case study in probabilistic thinking. A 62% win expectancy implies a 38% chance of the opposite outcome. That's not a rounding error; it's legitimate variance. The Marlins' lineup posted a .342 wOBA on the day against Atlanta's pitching, which sits in the 89th percentile of their seasonal performances. Sometimes regression finds the other guy first.

## Tomorrow's Top Pick Preview: Nationals Over Mets

Our Sep 26 model converges on Washington as the optimal selection at 62% confidence. The pitcher matchup heavily favors the home side: Connelly Early brings a superior K-BB% profile and significantly better park-adjusted metrics than Jonah Tong, whose road splits show meaningful platoon vulnerability.

## The Statistical Edge

Connelly Early's SIERA sits nearly half a run below Tong's, and his recent velocity trends suggest maintained stuff quality deep into September. Meanwhile, Tong's walk rate has climbed to 9.8% over his last four starts—exactly the kind of late-season command erosion our model weighs heavily. Add in Washington's superior defensive metrics at the positions that matter for Early's GB/FB profile, and you've got a multi-factor edge that compounds to our 62% projection.

The beauty of probabilistic forecasting is embracing the uncertainty while exploiting the edge. Tomorrow, that edge points to the Nationals.
